title: (b) the swap picker opens and lists faculty-scoped candidates
summary: A passing e2e that walks the Muster page's Fittings section: navigate to `/muster`, click into the Fittings tab so `StandingFittings` mounts, then click a gateway slot's Swap button. The picker that opens is the D9 library picker scoped to ONE faculty — a gateway slot only offers gateway candidates, because it lists the slot's own `candidates` array rather than the whole library.

states.label: /muster?composition=muster-standing-e2e
states.description: The Muster page is the shell-owned surface where the whole composition is configured. This flow exercises its Fittings section: the slot cards, the per-slot Swap trigger, and the picker that opens listing candidates scoped to that slot's faculty.

steps.title: The /muster route is a shim onto MusterPage
steps.description: Navigating to `/muster` lands on a server component that does nothing but mount `MusterPage`. All of the section-tab logic, data loading and the Standing Fittings panel live client-side inside that component — the route file itself is eight lines.

steps.title: The Fittings tab mounts StandingFittings
steps.description: Clicking `section-nav-fittings` sets the active section to `"fittings"`, and Muster's stage renders `StandingFittings` only for that section. The panels are lazy by tab, so the Standing Fittings grid — and its own `GET /api/muster/standing` fetch — does not exist until this click.

steps.title: StandingFittings owns its slot data
steps.description: `StandingFittings` fetches its own model from `GET /api/muster/standing` on mount, decoupled from the Duties payload. The response is a list of `slots`, and each slot already carries its `candidates` array — the faculty-scoped shortlist the picker will show. The client never filters the whole library; the server hands back one shortlist per slot.

steps.title: Swap sets the target to this slot's faculty
steps.description: Each fitting block renders a Swap button whose testid is `standing-swap-<faculty>-<fitting>` — here `standing-swap-gateway-http-gateway`. The test clicks it; `onSwap` fires with the fitting's id, which the parent turns into `setSwap({ faculty: slot.faculty, fromId })`. From this point the swap target is pinned to the gateway faculty, and that is what scopes everything downstream.

steps.title: The modal opens against the swap target's slot
steps.description: The swap target names a faculty; `swapSlot` looks up the matching slot by that faculty, and the `SwapModal` renders only when both the target and its slot exist. A gateway swap resolves to the gateway slot, so the modal that opens carries that one slot — never the library at large.

steps.title: The picker lists only that slot's candidates
steps.description: This is the climax the test asserts: the picker's result list is derived from `slot.candidates`, not from any global fitting index. With an empty search it IS `slot.candidates`; a query only narrows that same array. Because the slot was resolved from the gateway faculty, a gateway swap can only ever offer gateway fittings — the faculty scope is baked into the data, so the UI cannot leak an out-of-faculty candidate.
